items.title: Driven by LNG megaprojects, FDI reaches 1.88 billion dollars
items.summary: Maputo, 11 Nov (AIM) – The Bank of Mozambique, in its role as regulator of the national financial system, has recorded, in the first half of 2026, 1.88 billion US dollars as a result of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in the country. This figure corresponds to 33 percent of the amount attracted throughout 2025, mainly in the gas and mining sectors. According to data from Bank of Mozambique, this amount consists of inflows of 1.286 billion dollars in the first quarter of 2026 and 594.5 million dollars in the second quarter. The document points out that despite the slowdown observed between April and June, the structure of foreign investment remains largely dominated by megaprojects associated with natural resources, particularly natural gas, oil and mining, which continue to absorb most of the external capital directed towards the Mozambican economy.

items.summary: On Thursday Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Moscow and Dublin to hold talks with the Russian and Ukrainian presidents Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have concluded after a second day Although the American side said they saw "some openings", there was no hint of any breakthroughs to end the nearly five year-long war sparked by Russia's invasion However, both Moscow and Kyiv confirmed that a large-scale prisoner of war exchange was in the works and could be carried out soon Davyd Arakhamia from Ukraine's negotiating team said that this round of talks - the first since February - "was one of the hardest." items.title: Government to use big data to improve disaster preparedness
items.summary: Maputo, 11 Nov (AIM) – The Mozambican government plans to use artificial intelligence (AI) and Big Data to strengthen disaster preparedness, while prioritizing the expansion of broadband Internet access and the deployment of 5G technology as part of its digital transformation strategy. According to Américo Muchanga, minister of Communications and Digital Transformation, speaking on the sidelines of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference, taking place in Doha, from 9 to 12 November under the motto “A Connected Digital Future”, the government’s vision of building an inclusive, secure and sustainable digital society, is based on technological innovation and the use of information and communication technologies as tools for development. He identified the application of AI and Big Data in disaster prevention and management as a priority, aimed at improving the country’s ability to anticipate and respond to natural hazards.

items.title: Mozambique: Operators must improve communication to address fuel shortages in Tete — Notícias
items.summary: The recommendation was made on Wednesday afternoon, 11 November, after Mafumo heard from fuel station operators and visited the Moatize fuel depot. There, the Secretary of State found discrepancies in the procedures for requesting and supplying petroleum products. While fuel station managers point to bureaucratic difficulties at PETROMOC, the latter, in turn, highlights the need for those responsible for petrol stations to submit their orders further in advance in order to avoid stockouts During her interaction with the superintendent of the Moatize fuel depot, Cristina Mafumo revealed that a team from the central level was in the province conducting an investigation to better understand the reasons why motorists were spending long hours in queues, even spending the night at petrol stations, at a time when the depot continued to receive fuel Mafumo was assured that the situation could stabilise during the coming week

items.title: Spain sees widespread disruption in first general strike for 14 years
items.summary: Watch: Protesters gather across Spain for first general strike in 14 years Transport and other public services across Spain have faced serious disruption in the first general strike for 14 years called by the main unions over housing and the high cost of living Demonstrations have taken place across the country, including in Madrid and Barcelona, where tens of thousands marched in the evening Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant." However, the Spanish Confederation of Business Organisations said participation was "low and uneven", depending on the areas and sectors involved The general strike took place little more than two weeks ahead of national elections in Spain Some of the biggest disruption on Wednesday was seen in the main industrial hubs of Madrid and the north-eastern region of Catalonia where traffic was halted on several main roads The interior ministry said…

items.title: Egyptian journalist's retrial adjourned as UN warns of 'assaults on press freedom'
items.summary: Lina Attalah has said Egypt is "trying to limit the already-limited space" for independent media A criminal court in Cairo has postponed the retrial of the prominent Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah, whose case has drawn international condemnation Wednesday's opening hearing was adjourned until 18 November after defence lawyers representing the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr requested a new judge The UN has warned of "widening assaults on press freedom by Egyptian authorities, including the targeting, persecution and harassment of independent journalists" Attalah told the BBC that a recent crackdown was meant to "send a chilling message" to "the very few newsrooms that are left" She warned: "Everybody should be careful, everybody should be scared, everybody should be wondering if they are next." items.title: Integration of immigrants in Germany: Much has been accomplished but problems remain
items.summary: The Federal office for Migration and Refugees has released a new Integration Report. It found that while the integration of people with a migrant history is improving, violent youth remain a problem Few topics in Germany spark as many heated debates as integration. How successful have efforts been to integrate new arrivals? What is needed to enable successful integration? And what are the biggest problems? Every two years, the government's Commissioner for Integration presents a comprehensive set of statistics on the matter.
